plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the primary objective of the General Clauses Act, 1897?
options: To provide substantive criminal law procedures for all central acts
To shorten the language used in Central Acts and provide uniform rules of interpretation
To override the Constitution of India in matters of central legislation
To exclusively regulate the taxation powers of the Central and State Governments
plain.explanation: According to the ICAI study material, the General Clauses Act, 1897 is enacted to shorten the language of Central Acts, provide uniform definitions of frequently used terms, and lay down rules of interpretation to avoid repetition.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Does the General Clauses Act, 1897 apply to the Constitution of India?
options: Yes, fully and without any exception
No, it does not apply to the Constitution of India
Yes, but only to the Directive Principles of State Policy
Only when specifically notified by the President of India
plain.explanation: The General Clauses Act applies to all Central Acts and Regulations, but it does not apply to the Constitution of India, as the Constitution is the supreme law and has its own interpretation provisions.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(8) of the General Clauses Act, 1897, 'Central Government' in relation to anything done or to be done after the commencement of the Constitution means:
options: The President
The Prime Minister and the Union Cabinet
The Governor-General in Council
The President acting with the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
plain.explanation: Under Section 3(8)(b)(i), 'Central Government' in relation to anything done or to be done after the commencement of the Constitution means the President, who acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, but the statutory term refers to the President.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: An act is passed by Parliament on 10th January 2026, receives Presidential assent on 15th January 2026, and is published in the Official Gazette on 20th January 2026. The Act does not specify any particular date for its commencement. When will it come into operation?
options: 10th January 2026
15th January 2026
20th January 2026
15th February 2026
plain.explanation: Under Section 5 of the General Clauses Act, where an Act does not express any specific date of commencement, it comes into operation on the day on which it receives the assent of the President (i.e., 15th January 2026).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If a Central Act passed after the commencement of the Constitution is expressed to come into operation on a particular day, when does it commence?
options: At the sunrise on that day
At the expiration of the day preceding that day
At noon on that day
Seven days after that day
plain.explanation: Section 5 of the General Clauses Act provides that a Central Act comes into operation on the expiration of the day preceding the day on which it is expressed to come into force, unless a different intention is expressed.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the legal effect of the repeal of a Central Act under Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, unless a different intention appears?
options: It revives anything not in force or existing at the time the repeal takes effect
It affects any previous operation of any enactment so repealed or anything duly done or suffered thereunder
It does not affect any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed enactment
It automatically invalidates all pending legal proceedings instituted under the repealed act
plain.explanation: Section 6 protects accrued rights and liabilities. Specifically, the repeal does not affect any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed enactment, nor does it affect ongoing investigations or legal proceedings unless a contrary intention appears.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 6A of the General Clauses Act, where any Central Act repeals any enactment by which the text of any Central Act was amended, what is the status of the amendments?
options: The amendments automatically stand repealed along with the repealing act
The repeal of the amending enactment does not, unless a different intention appears, affect the continuance of any such amendment made by the enactment so repealed
The original unamended text revives immediately without any further notification
The amendments become voidable at the option of the Central Government
plain.explanation: According to Section 6A, the repeal of an amending Act does not affect the continuance of the amendment made by the repealed Act to the original legislation, unless a different intention appears.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: When an Act repeals and re-enacts with or without modification any provisions of a former enactment, references in any other enactment or instrument to the provisions so repealed shall, unless a different intention appears, be construed as references to:
options: The provisions so repealed
The provisions so re-enacted
The provisions of the Constitution of India
Null and void provisions
plain.explanation: Under Section 8 of the General Clauses Act, where an enactment is repealed and re-enacted, references to the repealed provisions in other enactments or instruments are construed as references to the provisions so re-enacted.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: According to Section 9 of the General Clauses Act, how are the words 'from' and 'to' interpreted when calculating time in a Central Act?
options: 'From' excludes the first day, and 'to' includes the last day
'From' includes the first day, and 'to' excludes the last day
Both 'from' and 'to' include the respective days
Both 'from' and 'to' exclude the respective days
plain.explanation: Section 9 lays down that in any Central Act, it shall be sufficient, for the purpose of excluding the first in a series of days or any other period of time, to use the word 'from', and for the purpose of including the last in a series of days or any other period of time, to use the word 'to'.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If a Central Act requires any document to be served by post, when is the service deemed to be effected, assuming proper addressing, prepaying, and posting under Section 27?
options: At the exact moment the letter is dropped in the post box
At the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post
Only when the recipient signs the acknowledgment card
Seven days after posting, irrespective of postal distance
plain.explanation: Section 27 states that where any legislation authorizes or requires document service by post, service is deemed to be effected by properly addressing, prepaying, and posting a registered letter, and, unless the contrary is proved, to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(22) of the General Clauses Act, 'Good Faith' is defined in civil law contexts. Which of the following best reflects the statutory meaning?
options: An act done honestly, whether it is done negligently or not
An act is deemed to be done in good faith where it is in fact done honestly, whether it is done negligently or not
An act done with absolute perfection and complete absence of any clerical error
An act done with due care and caution and never involving any negligence
plain.explanation: Under the General Clauses Act (Section 3(22)), a thing is deemed to be done in 'good faith' where it is in fact done honestly, whether it is done negligently or not. (Note: This contrasts with the Indian Penal Code definition which requires due care and attention).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What does Section 14 of the General Clauses Act provide regarding powers conferred on authorities?
options: Powers can be exercised only once and exhaust themselves
Powers conferred can be exercised from time to time as occasion requires
Powers can be exercised only with prior written permission of the Supreme Court
Powers lapse automatically after one year from the date of enactment
plain.explanation: Section 14 provides that where a power is conferred by any Central Act or Regulation, then that power may be exercised from time to time as occasion requires, unless a different intention appears.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 16 of the General Clauses Act, the power to make any appointment includes the power to:
options: Suspend or dismiss any person appointed, subject to any statutory conditions
Increase the salary of the appointee beyond budget limits
Transfer the appointee to a foreign country without consent
Exempt the appointee from criminal liability
plain.explanation: Section 16 states that the power to appoint includes the power to suspend or dismiss any person appointed by any such authority or officer, unless a different intention appears.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: According to Section 3(42) of the General Clauses Act, 'Person' includes:
options: Only natural human beings
Any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not
Only registered corporate entities and public sector undertakings
Foreign governments but not domestic companies
plain.explanation: Section 3(42) defines 'person' to include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, in addition to natural human beings.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(65) of the General Clauses Act, 'Year' shall mean a year reckoned according to:
options: The financial year commencing on 1st April
The British calendar (Gregorian calendar)
The Hindu Vikram Samvat calendar
The lunar calendar system
plain.explanation: Section 3(65) defines 'year' to mean a year reckoned according to the British calendar (Gregorian calendar).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the rule regarding gender and number under Section 13 of the General Clauses Act?
options: Words importing the masculine gender shall be taken to include females, and words in singular include plural and vice versa, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context
Masculine gender strictly excludes feminine gender unless explicitly stated otherwise
Singular words never include plural words under any circumstances
Neuter gender words apply exclusively to corporate entities
plain.explanation: Section 13 prescribes that in all Central Acts and Regulations, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, words importing the masculine gender include females, and words in the singular include the plural, and vice versa.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: When a Central Act confers power to make rules, regulations, or bye-laws, what does Section 21 imply regarding the power to amend, vary, or rescind them?
options: Rules made once can never be amended or rescinded by the same authority
The power to make includes the power to add to, amend, vary, or rescind rules, regulations, or bye-laws, subject to similar conditions
Only the judiciary can amend or rescind rules made by executive authorities
Rules can only be rescinded after approval by a public referendum
plain.explanation: Section 21 embodies the rule that the power to issue notifications, orders, rules, or bye-laws includes the power to add to, amend, vary, or rescind them, exercisable in the like manner and subject to the like sanction and conditions.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(26) of the General Clauses Act, 'Immovable property' includes:
options: Standing timber, growing crops, and grass
Land, benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth
Registered trademarks, patents, and copyrights
Money deposited in current bank accounts
plain.explanation: Section 3(26) defines 'immovable property' to include land, benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth, or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth (expressly excluding standing timber, growing crops, and grass).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(48) of the General Clauses Act, 'Registered', used with reference to a document, means registered under:
options: The Companies Act in force
The law for the time being in force for the registration of documents
The Reserve Bank of India guidelines
The Indian Stamp Act exclusively
plain.explanation: Section 3(48) defines 'registered' to mean registered under the law for the time being in force for the registration of documents (such as the Registration Act, 1908).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: According to Section 3(50) of the General Clauses Act, what does 'Schedule' mean?
options: A timetable for parliamentary debates
A schedule to the Central Act or Regulation in which the word occurs
An internal memo circulated by government departments
A financial budget document presented annually
plain.explanation: Section 3(50) defines 'Schedule' to mean a schedule to the Central Act or Regulation in which the word occurs.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: How is 'Oath' defined under Section 3(37) of the General Clauses Act?
options: A formal promise made exclusively in a religious ceremony
An oath shall include affirmation and declaration in the case of persons by law allowed to affirm or declare instead of swearing
A signed written undertaking submitted to a police officer
A secret pledge taken by political party members
plain.explanation: Section 3(37) defines 'Oath' to include affirmation and declaration in the case of persons by law allowed to affirm or declare instead of swearing.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the effect of an act being done on a 'holiday' as per Section 10 of the General Clauses Act, where an act or proceeding is directed or allowed to be done in any court or office on a certain day or within a prescribed period?
options: The act becomes permanently void and cannot be performed
If the court or office is closed on that day, the act or proceeding shall be considered as done in due time if it is done on the next day afterwards on which the court or office is open
The period is shortened by one day to adjust for the holiday
A penalty is automatically levied on the person obligated to perform the act
plain.explanation: Section 10 provides that if any act or proceeding is directed or allowed to be done in any court or office on a certain day or within a prescribed period, then, if the court or office is closed on that day or the last day of the period, the act/proceeding shall be deemed in time if done on the next day the court/office is open.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(23) of the General Clauses Act, what does 'Government' or 'the Government' include?
options: Only the Central Government
Both the Central Government and any State Government
Only municipal corporations and local authorities
Foreign governments recognized by India
plain.explanation: Section 3(23) defines 'Government' or 'the Government' to include both the Central Government and any State Government.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: In construing a statutory provision, if two interpretations are possible, one of which validates the provision while the other renders it redundant or unconstitutional, which rule or principle guides the courts?
options: Literal interpretation strictly without looking at consequences
Principle of Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat (it is better for a thing to have effect than to be made void)
Automatic reliance on administrative circulars
Strict penal interpretation in favor of the prosecution
plain.explanation: Under canons of statutory interpretation supported by general principles and the General Clauses Act framework, courts prefer an interpretation that makes the legislation effective and workable rather than one that renders it void or redundant.
conceptTags: Ut Res Magis Valeat Quam Pereat

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(54) of the General Clauses Act, 'Sign' with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, with reference to a person who is unable to write his name, includes:
options: Making his thumb impression or mark upon the document
Verbally authorizing a third party to forge the signature
Leaving the signature column completely blank
Submitting a photograph instead of a signature
plain.explanation: Wait, let's verify Section 3(56) or 3(54): Under Section 3(56), 'Sign', with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, shall, with reference to a person who is unable to write his name, include his mark, with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If a Central Act confers power to appoint a public officer, what does Section 15 state regarding the appointment by name or office?
options: Appointments must always be made by personal name only
Appointments may be made either by name or by virtue of office
Appointments must be made exclusively through competitive civil services examinations
Appointments cannot be made by office under any circumstances
plain.explanation: Section 15 specifies that where a Central Act confers a power to appoint any public officer, such appointment may be made either by name or by virtue of office.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(43) of the General Clauses Act, what is the definition of 'Political Agent'?
options: An elected member of Parliament representing a constituency
The principal officer appointed by the Central Government to exercise political functions in a specified territory
A registered lobbyist hired by corporate entities
Any spokesperson of a recognized political party
plain.explanation: Section 3(43) defines 'Political Agent' as the principal officer appointed by the Central Government to exercise political functions in any territory outside India or within India as notified.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following sections of the General Clauses Act deals with the recovery of fines?
options: Section 25
Section 6
Section 10
Section 27
plain.explanation: Section 25 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 deals with the recovery of fines, providing that sections 63 to 70 of the Indian Penal Code and the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall apply to such recovery.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the legal implication when an Act repeals any enactment and provides substantive new provisions without saving clauses?
options: Section 6 of the General Clauses Act automatically operates to save accrued rights, liabilities, and pending legal proceedings, unless a different intention appears
All previous liabilities and penalties are completely wiped out without exception
Pending suits are transferred to the executive branch of government
The repealing act becomes null and void ab initio
plain.explanation: Section 6 acts as a statutory safety net. Even if a repealing act does not contain express saving clauses, Section 6 applies unless a different intention appears in the repealing enactment.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 3(13) of the General Clauses Act, 'Commencement' used with reference to an Act or Regulation means:
options: The day on which the Bill is first introduced in Parliament
The day on which the Act or Regulation comes into operation
The day on which the President signs the assent document
The day on which the notification is drafted by the ministry
plain.explanation: Section 3(13) defines 'Commencement' with reference to an Act or Regulation to mean the day on which the Act or Regulation comes into operation.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: The Parliament of India passed the 'Commercial Enterprises (Regulation) Act, 2025'. The Act did not specify any date of commencement in its text. It received the assent of the President on 12th November 2025 and was published in the Official Gazette on 18th November 2025. Section 45 of the Act empowered the Central Government to frame rules for commercial registration. On 1st December 2025, the Central Government framed Commercial Rules, 2025. Later, due to industry feedback, the Central Government sought to amend these rules on 10th January 2026.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the exact date of commencement of the Commercial Enterprises (Regulation) Act, 2025?
options: 12th November 2025
18th November 2025
1st December 2025
1st January 2026
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 5 of the General Clauses Act, where an Act does not express a specific date of commencement, it comes into operation on the day on which it receives the assent of the President, which is 12th November 2025.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under which section of the General Clauses Act does the Central Government derive the power to amend or rescind the Commercial Rules, 2025?
options: Section 14
Section 16
Section 21
Section 27
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 21 of the General Clauses Act provides that the power to make rules, regulations, notifications, or bye-laws includes the power to add to, amend, vary, or rescind them.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Suppose the Commercial Enterprises (Regulation) Act, 2025 was expressed to come into force on '1st December 2025'. According to Section 5, when exactly would it take effect?
options: At sunrise on 1st December 2025
At the expiration of 30th November 2025
At noon on 1st December 2025
At midnight between 1st and 2nd December 2025
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 5 specifies that where a Central Act is expressed to come into operation on a particular day, it shall come into operation on the expiration of the day preceding that day.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If the Central Government exercises its rule-making power multiple times as occasions arise under the Act, which section validates such continuous exercise?
options: Section 14
Section 6
Section 8
Section 13
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 14 establishes that where a power is conferred by a Central Act, such power may be exercised from time to time as occasion requires.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: M/s Apex Traders, a partnership firm, entered into a statutory contract regulated by the 'Industrial Development Act, 2018'. In 2024, Parliament repealed the Industrial Development Act, 2018 and enacted the 'New Industrial Enterprises Act, 2024', which contained provisions re-enacting several clauses of the old Act with modifications. Prior to the repeal, M/s Apex Traders had incurred a liability of Rs. 5,00,000 under the old Act. The repealing Act did not contain any specific saving clause regarding past liabilities.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the legal status of the liability of Rs. 5,00,000 incurred by M/s Apex Traders under the repealed Act?
options: The liability is automatically extinguished because the old Act was repealed without a saving clause
Under Section 6, the liability is saved, and M/s Apex Traders remains liable despite the repeal
The liability is transferred to the State Government treasury
The liability becomes voidable at the discretion of the firm
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 6 of the General Clauses Act provides that repeal does not affect any liability incurred under the repealed enactment, unless a different intention appears, operating as a statutory saving clause.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: How shall references in other existing contracts to the provisions of the repealed Industrial Development Act, 2018 be construed after the enactment of the New Industrial Enterprises Act, 2024?
options: As references to nothing, rendering the contracts void
As references to the provisions so re-enacted under the New Industrial Enterprises Act, 2024, under Section 8
As references exclusively to the Constitution of India
As references to state-level municipal bylaws
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 8 of the General Clauses Act, where an enactment is repealed and re-enacted, references in other enactments or instruments to the repealed provisions shall be construed as references to the provisions so re-enacted.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under the General Clauses Act, how is 'M/s Apex Traders' (a partnership firm) classified when the term 'Person' is used in the statute?
options: It is excluded from the definition of person
It is included under 'Person' as an association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not
It is classified strictly as a government department
It is recognized only if registered under the Companies Act
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 3(42) defines 'person' to include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, which covers partnership firms.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If M/s Apex Traders consists of partners, how does Section 13 apply regarding gender and number in the interpretation of the Act?
options: Masculine terms apply only to male partners
Words importing the masculine gender include females, and singular includes plural, unless repugnant to the context
Singular words strictly exclude plural partners
Neuter gender applies exclusively to corporate partners
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 13 dictates that unless repugnant to the subject or context, words importing masculine gender include females and singular words include plural and vice versa.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Mr. Vikram, a businessman, was served with a statutory notice issued by a regulatory authority under a Central Act requiring him to submit compliance documents within 30 days. The notice was sent via registered post, properly addressed and prepaid, on 1st March 2026. Due to postal delays, the letter reached Mr. Vikram on 10th March 2026. The 30th day for submission fell on Sunday, 31st March 2026, on which date the regulatory office was completely closed for a public holiday.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act, when is the service of the statutory notice deemed to have been effected on Mr. Vikram?
options: On 10th March 2026 when he physically received it
At the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post
On 1st March 2026 the moment it was handed to the post office
Only after Mr. Vikram files an acknowledgment receipt
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 27 states that service is deemed to be effected by properly addressing, prepaying, and posting a registered letter, and to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: According to Section 10 of the General Clauses Act, since the office was closed on Sunday, 31st March 2026, by when must Mr. Vikram submit the compliance documents?
options: On Saturday, 30th March 2026
On the next day afterwards on which the office is open (i.e., Monday, 1st April 2026)
He is granted an automatic extension of 30 additional days
The notice stands lapsed and cannot be complied with
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 10 provides that if the prescribed period ends on a day on which the court or office is closed, the act is considered done in due time if performed on the next day the office is open.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: When calculating the 30-day period starting 'from' 1st March 2026, how is the first day treated under Section 9 of the General Clauses Act?
options: 1st March 2026 is excluded from the calculation
1st March 2026 is fully included in the calculation
Two days are added as penalty for starting on the 1st
The calculation is based on the lunar calendar
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 9, the use of the word 'from' excludes the first day in a series of days or period of time.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If the statutory time period expired on the last day, and that day was reckoned according to the British calendar, which section defines 'Year' or 'Calendar' in this context?
options: Section 3(65)
Section 3(26)
Section 3(42)
Section 3(13)
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 3(65) defines 'year' to mean a year reckoned according to the British calendar.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: The Central Board of Excise and Customs issued an order appointing Mr. Sharma as a 'Special Adjudication Officer' by virtue of his office as Joint Commissioner. Six months later, the Board decided to suspend Mr. Sharma pending an inquiry into administrative irregularities. Mr. Sharma challenged the suspension, arguing that the appointing authority did not possess the power to suspend him once appointed without a separate disciplinary statute.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under Section 16 of the General Clauses Act, does the power to make an appointment include the power to suspend or dismiss?
options: No, suspension requires a separate constitutional amendment
Yes, the power to appoint includes the power to suspend or dismiss any person appointed, unless a different intention appears
Only dismissal is included, while suspension is strictly prohibited
Only the High Court can suspend a public officer appointed by the Board
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 16 expressly lays down that the power to appoint includes the power to suspend or dismiss the person appointed, unless a different intention appears in the enactment.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under Section 15 of the General Clauses Act, was the Board's appointment of Mr. Sharma 'by virtue of his office' legally valid?
options: No, public officers must always be appointed by personal name only
Yes, appointments under Central Acts may be made either by name or by virtue of office
Only the President of India can make appointments by virtue of office
Appointments by office are void ab initio
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 15 specifies that where a Central Act confers power to appoint any public officer, such appointment may be made either by name or by virtue of office.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Mr. Sharma acted honestly in an administrative decision, although he committed a minor procedural negligence, how is 'Good Faith' evaluated under Section 3(22) of the General Clauses Act?
options: It is not in good faith because negligence was present
It is deemed to be done in good faith if it is in fact done honestly, whether negligent or not
Good faith requires absolute perfection without any procedural error
Good faith is determined exclusively by police investigation reports
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 3(22) defines good faith under the General Clauses Act as anything done honestly, whether done negligently or not.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If the order appointing Mr. Sharma was notified in the Official Gazette, what does Section 3(39) generally define 'Official Gazette' to mean?
options: Any privately published newspaper in the district
The Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State
Social media handles of government ministries
Annual reports published by corporate bodies
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 3(39) defines 'Official Gazette' to mean the Gazette of India or the Official Gazette of a State, as applicable.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: An economic legislation enacted by Parliament contained provisions penalizing tax evasion, including the imposition of substantial financial fines. A corporate entity, Zeta Ltd., was found guilty of violating the statute. Zeta Ltd. contended that since the company is an artificial legal person and not a natural human being, penal fines and criminal provisions under the Act should not apply to it. Furthermore, the company owned a commercial warehouse built permanently on land, which the tax authorities sought to attach as immovable property.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under Section 3(42) of the General Clauses Act, does the term 'Person' include Zeta Ltd., an artificial corporate body?
options: No, 'person' strictly refers to living human beings
Yes, 'person' includes any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not
Only public sector companies are included under 'person'
Foreign companies are included, but domestic companies are excluded
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 3(42) defines 'person' to include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or not.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: How is Zeta Ltd.'s commercial warehouse permanently fastened to the earth classified under Section 3(26) of the General Clauses Act?
options: Movable property because it is a commercial asset
Immovable property because it includes things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth
Intangible property like a trademark
Standing timber
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 3(26) defines 'immovable property' to include land, benefits arising out of land, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which section of the General Clauses Act governs the recovery of fines imposed on Zeta Ltd. under the Central Act?
options: Section 25
Section 6
Section 27
Section 10
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 25 of the General Clauses Act specifically deals with the recovery of fines, making provisions of the IPC and CrPC applicable to such recovery.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If the Act used words importing the singular number with respect to offending directors of Zeta Ltd., how does Section 13 apply?
options: Singular words strictly apply to only one director and never more
Words in the singular include the plural and vice versa, unless repugnant to the context
Plural words require explicit re-enactment by Parliament
Singular words apply exclusively to female directors
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 13 prescribes that words in the singular include the plural and vice versa, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context.
